  MIT BLR - BTech VI Semester - End Semester Makeup Examination - June -2024  
  Machine Learning [CSE-4032]  
  Marks: 50                                                                               Duration: 180 mins.  
  PART-A  
  Answer all the questions.  
  1)           Compare and contrast classification and regression tasks in machine learning. Provide  
  examples of each type of task and discuss the specific objectives and evaluation metrics  
  (5)  
  associated with them  
  A)  
  B)      Evaluate the effectiveness of ensemble methods such as bagging and boosting in  
  improving the robustness and accuracy of machine learning models. Discuss how these         (5)  
  methods combine multiple base learners to overcome individual weaknesses.  
  
  2)           Contrast the mathematical principles behind PCA and ICA and explain how they lead to  
  distinct methods for dimensionality reduction and signal separation? What advantages  
  (5)  
  and limitations do these mathematical approaches offer in real-world scenarios.  
  A)  
  B)      Explore the concept of kernel trick and its significance in SVM. How does the kernel  
  trick enable SVM to efficiently handle high-dimensional feature spaces without  
  explicitly computing the transformation? Can you provide insights into the mathematical (5)  
  intuition behind the kernel trick.  
  
  3)           Assess the limitations of K-means clustering and propose alternative clustering  
  algorithms that address these limitations. Evaluate the performance of the proposed  
  algorithms in terms of scalability, robustness, and ability to handle non-linear data       (5)  
  A)      distributions.  
  
  B)      Analyze the relationship between the bias-variance tradeoff and model complexity. How  
  does increasing model complexity affect the bias and variance components of the error, (5)  
  and how does this impact the overall model performance.  
  
  4)           Analyze the challenges of applying reinforcement learning algorithms in real-world  
  scenarios with large state and action spaces. Discuss strategies for dealing with the curse  
  of dimensionality and improving the efficiency of value function approximation and          (5)  
  A)      policy search methods.  
  
  B)      Compare and Contrast value iteration and policy iteration algorithms. How does the  
  choice of discount factor affect the convergence and stability of these algorithms.         (5)  
  
  5)           Evaluate the impact of data imbalance on the performance of classification algorithms    (5)  
  such as logistic regression and support vector machines. Discuss techniques for handling
